---
description: Convert and register one immutable intake batch.
agent: agent
---

Treat `--create` and `--submit` as mutually exclusive modes.

## Create mode

Use this mode only when the invocation contains `--create`. Do not require an
issue reference because the Intake issue does not exist yet. Invoke
`intake-creation`.

Operate as a conversational wizard. Ask for one missing value at a time:
customer/workstream, intake date, one source file path, whether to add another
file, known ambiguities/priorities/exclusions, optional planned completion, and
final confirmation. Loop over source files one path at a time. Parameters
already supplied in the invocation skip their questions.

Validate every file before accepting it, but do not copy or modify files until
final confirmation. After confirmation, copy the exact bytes under
`intake/<customer-slug>/<yyyy-mm-dd>/`, create a focused branch and commit, push
it, and open the source-evidence PR with the required
`d365-intake-evidence` metadata block. Do not create the Intake issue directly,
and do not approve or merge the PR. Merge automation creates the Intake issue
with commit-pinned links.

## Existing issue modes

When `--create` is absent, require one explicit GitHub Intake issue reference,
either an issue number such as `#4` or the issue URL. If it is missing, stop
immediately and ask the Business Analyst to provide the Intake issue number. Do
not search for, list, infer, or select an issue from repository state,
conversation history, recent activity, or open issues.

After the Business Analyst provides the reference, verify that the issue exists
and is an Intake work order. Then select exactly one mode:

## Prepare mode

Use this mode when both `--create` and `--submit` are absent. Read
`conventions.yml`, repository context, and the issue. Invoke
`intake-conversion` and `intake-traceability`.
Download each commit-pinned issue-linked source from GitHub into a fresh
operating-system temporary directory through the authenticated GitHub MCP or
Contents API, decoding base64 content directly to bytes. Do not try an
anonymous raw endpoint for a private repository, and never convert a workspace
copy. Preserve raw evidence, create only derived evidence and the `INTK-####`
registry entry, validate provenance, clean up the temporary directory, and stop
for Business Analyst review without committing or opening a pull request.

After presenting the completed validation and review summary, ask exactly one
question: whether the Business Analyst wants to submit the reviewed intake now.
Do not ask before the review summary, and do not treat the original prepare
invocation as submission consent. If the answer is no, absent, or unclear, stop
with the reviewed files uncommitted. If the answer is explicitly yes, continue
into Submit mode.

## Submit mode

Use this mode when the invocation contains `--submit` or when the Business
Analyst explicitly accepts the post-review submission prompt. Treat either
action as confirmation that the Business Analyst completed the local evidence
review; it does not approve the intake-acceptance gate.

Resolve exactly one `INTK-####` registry row linked to the supplied issue and
require its status to be `Evidence Review`. Do not reconvert evidence or modify
authored files. Revalidate the permanent links, commit IDs, recorded SHA-256
values, conversion diagnostics, provenance, and derived Markdown files. Stop if
the intake is missing, ambiguous, incomplete, or already submitted.

Create a focused branch and stage only `intake/_index.md` plus the derived
Markdown files for that intake. Never stage raw source documents, local
temporary files, `audit/`, or unrelated changes. Check the staged diff before
committing. Commit, push, and open one pull request whose title identifies the
intake and whose body contains `Closes #<issue-number>`, the `INTK-####`,
permanent source links, SHA-256 values, validation results, and an unchecked
intake-acceptance checklist. If an open pull request already exists for the
same issue and intake, report it instead of creating a duplicate. Stop before
approval or merge.
